title: Node-separation decay loop is dead code; effective separation (0.0625 rad) contradicts the documented hitbox-disjoint contract
evidence:
const MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD := 0.25 # keeps node hitboxes (r 0.95) from overlapping
const MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR := 0.25 # fallback keeps at least 25% of the separation
...
		var sep := MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR * (1.0 - float(attempt) / 80.0) * MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD
		if sep < MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25:
			sep = MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25
detail: 0.25*(1-a/80)*0.25 <= 0.0625 for every attempt, so the floor clamp pins sep to a constant 0.0625: the 80-attempt decay machinery never engages, and 0.0625 rad (0.5 units at R=8) is below the ~0.24 rad needed to keep r=0.95 hitboxes disjoint as the comment/spec claim.
recommended_fix: Use sep = MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * (1.0 - 0.75*attempt/80.0) so it decays 0.25 -> 0.0625, and fix the misleading comment/constant name (MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR reads like a typo).

title: Geodesic's 'pure static math' module takes/returns scene-tree Node3D in snap_candidate
detail: The module's stated contract (and the spec code map: 'pure static math') is violated: snap_candidate is scene-aware, coupling the math layer to Node3D and forcing the headless snap test to stage real nodes in the tree.
recommended_fix: Accept Array of Vector3 positions (or a position Callable) and return the winning index; let the caller map index -> node. Keeps Geodesic tree-free.

title: Scripts self-resolve sibling scene paths instead of composition-root injection
detail: main.gd is documented as the composition root wiring signals, yet dependencies are hard-coded via relative paths in three scripts (inconsistently: router reaches ../OrbitRig/Camera3D directly while the controller uses rig.camera). Renaming/reparenting nodes in main.tscn breaks scripts at runtime.
recommended_fix: Have main.gd inject dependencies (setup(rig, nodes, pipes) or exported NodePaths) so the scene layout lives in one place; route both camera accesses through the OrbitCamera abstraction.

title: Dev-only capture harness is instantiated inside the shipped main scene
evidence:
[node name="CaptureRunner" type="Node" parent="."]
script = ExtResource("7")
--- capture_runner.gd: "## Capture harness (A4): INERT during normal play — activates only when the game is launched with `-- --capture`."
detail: Proof-of-look tooling (reads sibling nodes, commits pipes, quits the tree) ships in the game scene tree. Flag-gated and inert in play, but it mixes dev/proof concerns into the production composition and every scene load pays its _ready.
recommended_fix: Move capture sequencing to a separate overlay scene or a --script harness that instantiates main.tscn, keeping the shipped scene free of tooling nodes.

title: draw_move's 1e-4 rebuild guard is a no-op at real zooms — preview rebuilds on every motion event anyway
evidence:
# Rebuild the preview mesh only when the arc end actually moved — motion
	# events arrive per-frame and a full SurfaceTool rebuild per event churns.
	if end.distance_to(_last_preview_end) > 1e-4:
		_last_preview_end = end
		_show_preview(_source.global_position, end)
		_preview.visible = true
detail: At the globe stop (distance 22, fov 50, 900px tall) one pixel of pointer motion projects to ~0.023 world units — 200x the 1e-4 threshold — so the full SurfaceTool rebuild still fires on essentially every motion event. The guard adds state (_last_preview_end) and complexity without the claimed benefit.
recommended_fix: Either quantize the projection (e.g. snap end to the geodesic sample grid or ~1px-equivalent arc step) so the guard actually dedupes, or drop the guard and the _last_preview_end state.

title: Geodesic.ray_sphere ships in production but is only exercised by tests
evidence:
static func ray_sphere(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, center: Vector3, radius: float) -> Vector3:
--- only callers: ./tests/test_geodesic.gd:79-83 (production ray-casts use physics: connect_controller.gd _project_pointer / input_router.gd _pick)
detail: A second, analytic ray/projection path exists solely to be tested while gameplay uses physics ray-casts. Dead production surface that E2+ readers must reason about, and the two projection paths can silently diverge.
recommended_fix: Either use the analytic ray_sphere for the pointer projection (cheap, collider-free) or delete it and its test until needed.

title: Orthonormal-basis idiom and elevated_path computation duplicated across modules
evidence:
node_site.gd: var helper := Vector3.UP if absf(n.dot(Vector3.UP)) < 0.99 else Vector3.RIGHT / var t1 := n.cross(helper).normalized() / var t2 := t1.cross(n).normalized()
--- pipe_arc.gd:117-119: same three lines verbatim (dir variant)
--- pipe_arc.gd:46 and :105: identical `Geodesic.elevated_path(_a, _b, WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS, BASE_ELEVATION_FRAC * WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS * _radius_scale, SEGMENTS)` computed once for the mesh and again for the trestles
detail: The same basis-from-normal construction is copy-pasted in two files, and build() recomputes the identical 49-point path twice per rebuild. Small now, but the idiom will spread (E3 props, E2 packet paths) and the copies can drift.
recommended_fix: Extract Geodesic.basis_from_normal(n) (or a small BasisUtil) and have build() compute the path once, passing it to _rebuild_mesh and _rebuild_trestles.

title: Pipe-bundle registry keys bundles by node display names
detail: Bundle identity depends on tree node-name strings staying unique forever. E3 growth adds/removes nodes dynamically; a renamed, recycled, or duplicated name silently merges or orphans bundles — name uniqueness is an implicit invariant nothing enforces.
recommended_fix: Key by instance identity (get_instance_id() pair or NodeSite references via a stable id field assigned at staging) instead of display names.
